o: Swap at most one contiguous subarray between nums1 and nums2, then maximize the larger array sum. Swapping a range changes sum(nums2) by sum(d) where d[i] = nums1[i] - nums2[i]; so the best swap for nums2's benefit is the maximum-subarray sum of d (Kadane), and symmetrically for nums1 with -d. The answer is max(sum1, sum2, sum2 + kadane(d), sum1 + kadane(-d)). Empty swaps are covered by the raw sums. Example 3 confirms no-swap can win.
k: Swapping [l..r] adds sum of d = nums1 - nums2 over the range to sum(nums2).
Best single swap = Kadane's maximum subarray of d (and of -d for the other direction).
Not swapping is always allowed, so include the untouched sums as candidates.

a.n: Approach 1: Kadane on the difference array
a.i: Reduce the choice of swap range to the classic maximum subarray problem on d and on -d. Kadane runs in O(n) with O(1) memory; combine with the base sums for the final maximum.
s: Build d[i] = nums1[i] - nums2[i]; run Kadane to get best positive-gain subarray g.
Candidate scores: s1, s2, s2 + g, s1 + kadane(-d).
a.t: O(n) — two linear scans (sums plus two Kadane passes).
a.sp: O(n) for the difference arrays, or O(1) if fused into one pass.

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix sums with running minimum
a.i: The best gain of swapping into nums2 is max over r of (prefD[r] - min prefD[0..r-1]). Tracking the prefix sum and its running minimum in one pass is algebraically identical to Kadane but framed via prefixes, which some find easier to derive and prove.
s: Iterate computing running prefix of d and its minimum so far.
Best gain = max(pref - minPref) over all positions.
Apply symmetrically to -d for swaps favoring nums1.
Combine with s1, s2 and return the max.
a.sp: O(n) for difference arrays (O(1) if streamed).

w: Kadane framing is the quickest to explain in an interview. Pitfalls: allowing empty ranges is fine (raw sums cover it), but ensure Kadane permits zero-length results (initialize best = 0); use 64-bit sums since n * 1e4 reaches 1e9. Follow-up: k disjoint swaps, or swapping to minimize the maximum sum.
